To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy budget of the atmosphere can be decomposed into three parts, namely the energy budget of an idealized atmosphere, the energy budget of atmospheric waves, and the energy budget of diabatic heating.

(1) the APE and KE budgets are not closed in the atmosphere; (2) the APE budget can be closed by including the effect of the surface pressure gradient; (3) the KE budget can be closed in the atmosphere if the effect of the pressure gradient on the KE convergence is included; (4) the APE is not a conserved quantity; and (5) the KE is not a conservative quantity.

the energy fluxes and the entropy production of an atmosphere can be decomposed into contributions from the mean and the fluctuations of temperature and wind, and that the entropy production of a stably stratified atmosphere can be decomputed into contributions from the eddy fluxes of heat, momentum, and potential energy.
